title: Ready to try presents features to play with, not a list of three hundred file names
goal: Ready to try hands you a menu of three hundred entries and asks you to pick one. That is a file list, not a place to discover what is new. Rebuild it as a proper surface: what landed most recently comes first, grouped by the part of the app it belongs to, each one a card carrying its name, the one line saying what you can now do, and how long trying it takes. A card opens in place to reveal the steps, the questions it wants answered and what is still rough, so the page starts quiet and goes deep only where you ask. Nothing is hidden behind a control you have to operate before you can see anything at all.
notes: Asked for by the user on 2026-09-07: the select with three hundred items is not a design, and they want progressive disclosure on a surface that reads as a polished professional dashboard. Today auditPicker (docs/design/mocks/pages/dashboard.html line 1198) builds a single select of every file name and renderAudits draws one report below it. There are 325 reports and they already carry what a card needs: feature, epic, summary, setup, try, evaluate and rough. The epic is the grouping, and recent ones spread across ui-building, ui-components, ui-layout, measure-redline and unmanned-loop, so grouping by it is meaningful rather than decorative. Two things to get right that a naive rebuild will miss. First the data: the state payload deliberately carries only audit NAMES and each report is fetched when opened, so a card list needs the summary line without fetching all of them; either widen what the state carries for the recent set only, or fetch lazily as cards come into view, and say which in the audit. Second, the reports are dated by file name, so ordering and the landed date should come from that rather than from reading each file. Keep the reaction machinery untouched, since that is what turns a comment into a task.
acceptance: Arriving at Ready to try shows something immediately: the newest reports as cards, with no menu to operate first
Each card shows the feature name, the single sentence saying what you can now do, when it landed, and how many steps trying it takes
Cards are grouped by the part of the app they belong to, newest first, with the count in each group visible
Opening a card reveals its steps, its questions and what is still rough, in place, without leaving the page or losing your position
Only one card needs to be open at a time, and closing returns you to exactly where you were in the list
Anything older than the recent set is reachable, by searching by name and by filtering to a part of the app, but never as the first thing you meet
The whole page is usable from the keyboard, and every card and control has a name a screen reader can read
Reacting to a line still works exactly as it does now, and a reaction still becomes a task
It stays fast with three hundred reports and more: the page does not fetch every report to draw the list, and the audit gives a measured load time
The design follows the dashboard's own language rather than inventing controls, and the audit says which existing pieces were reused
Audit written under queue/audits/ with the page on arrival, a card open, and a search, anything rough filed as a follow-up

log.note: Adversarial pass before building. The mock said nothing here, the task did, and two of its instructions were wrong on contact. (1) The goal asks the card to say 'how long trying it takes'; there is no honest time in a report, so the card says the step count, which the acceptance list already asked for and which is real. (2) Grouping by the audit's own epic would have made eleven groups, two of them named things like 'Using the arrow tool to point to something should make it easy to create a legible caption in a pill with a shadow', which is a whole sentence, not a section. Rolled each epic up to its top-level ancestor in objectives.json instead, giving four groups that are genuinely 'the part of the app': building UI, redlining, the loop, the design system. Cut as decorative: a time estimate, per-area colour pips, a thumbnail on a closed card.

Data. Widened neither the state poll nor the client: a new /api/audit-index returns header fields only (name, date, feature, epic, summary, steps, questions, rough) for every report, built server-side and cached until the audits directory changes. Measured: 333 reports parse in 9ms cold, 1ms warm, 152KB over the wire in 2 to 5ms, fetched ONCE per page and again only when the report count moves. Bodies still load one at a time from /api/audit/<name> when a card opens. The day and the sort order come from the file name, so nothing is read to draw the list.

Adversarial pass on the built thing, on the real dashboard in a browser. Fixed what it found: the card header repeated the page title (renamed to 'Everything the loop has finished'); the summary at --faint was about 2.9:1 on the light panel (moved to --dim); the setup line collided with the first section heading (the body is a flex column with a real gap now); the comment control was invisible to a keyboard because it only appeared on hover (:focus-visible now shows it); narrowing the search left an invisible card 'open', holding the live poll (the filter closes it); Escape did nothing (it now backs out of the composer, then the card).

Verified, not assumed. Arrival draws 24 cards in 3 groups with no control operated. Header scroll anchoring measured: opening and closing a card leaves its header at the same pixel (48.89 before, during and after) and restores scrollTop exactly. Keyboard: Tab reaches select, search and every card; Return opens; Escape closes; aria-expanded flips. Show all 333 draws in 54ms and fetches zero images because closed cards have no body. Reaction path filed a real task from a real line with the right audit, anchor, quote and epic, then dropped it. Checked in dark and light and at 820px. Scripts/test.sh green (4494 tests). check-reserved.mjs clean. New audit-index-drill.mjs passes. decision-drill.mjs is flaky on an unchanged tree too (4 of 6 failures with the change stashed), filed separately.

Found on the way, filed not fixed: /api/state is 3,043,595 bytes every 4 seconds, 2.5MB of it task logs (the-dashboard-downloads-three-megabytes-every-fo); decision-drill.mjs is timing-flaky (the-decision-drill-fails-about-half-the-time-on).

Ready to try opens on the newest 24 reports as cards grouped by pillar epic (docs/design/mocks/pages/dashboard.html), each with feature name, summary, day landed and step count; a card opens in place with scroll anchored to its header. New /api/audit-index (queue-lib.mjs + dev-server.mjs) draws the list in one 152KB request, 2-5ms, cached; bodies still load per card. Verified in a browser on the real dashboard: arrival, open/close scroll anchoring measured, keyboard Tab/Return/Escape, search across all 333, area filter, Show all in 54ms, and a real reaction filed a task then dropped. Dark and light, 820px. Scripts/test.sh green, check-reserved clean, new audit-index-drill.mjs passes. Audit: queue/audits/2026-09-07-ready-to-try-cards.json
